user_message: Earlier you said airplane wings need longer airflow over the curved top, so the air must move faster to reunite at the trailing edge. I remain unconvinced. Revise the explanation and give one test that distinguishes the stories.
allowed_evidence: Air parcels split at a wing's leading edge are not required to reunite simultaneously. Wing shape, angle of attack, circulation, and the resulting pressure field redirect air downward and exert an upward force on the wing.
public_rubric: Replaces it with a causal account involving pressure and momentum change.
Provides an observation that discriminates between explanations.
Avoids substituting a new absolute rule.
